title: Divergent Orbital Diamagnetism from Chiral Edge States in Chern Insulators
abstract: Two-dimensional massless Dirac systems, exemplified by graphene, are known to exhibit a divergent orbital diamagnetic susceptibility that scales linearly with system size. Motivated by viewing a chiral edge state as one half of an enlarged analogue of a benzene ring, we study Chern insulators under open boundary conditions and find the same divergent scaling. This giant diamagnetism is robust against disorder, revealing its topological nature. Our results further suggest a profound connection to the divergent diamagnetism of massless Dirac systems.
summary: This work analyzes the orbital diamagnetism in Chern insulators using lattice models, finding that the susceptibility diverges linearly with system size when open boundary conditions are applied. This giant diamagnetism is robust against disorder and is attributed to the topological nature of the chiral edge states, distinguishing it sharply from the finite response predicted by bulk theory.
main_problem: The study investigates whether orbital diamagnetism can distinguish between topologically non-trivial (Chern insulator) and trivial massive Dirac insulators, focusing on the role of chiral edge states.
main_result: Both Chern insulators and massless Dirac systems exhibit giant diamagnetism that scales linearly with system size under open boundary conditions, a feature absent in the bulk calculation or trivial insulators.
method: The authors use numerical calculations of the normalized orbital susceptibility derived from the total energy dependence on magnetic flux, comparing open and periodic boundary conditions.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using a lattice massive Dirac Hamiltonian, specifically the Qi–Wu–Zhang (QWZ) model, applied to Chern insulators and related Dirac systems on a square lattice.
key_observables: Orbital diamagnetic susceptibility ($\chi_{	ext{orb}}$ or $\chi_{	ext{norm}}$), and its scaling with system size ($L$).
important_parameters: System size ($L$), magnetic flux ($\phi$), mass term ($m$), and disorder strength ($w$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes zero temperature and fixed particle number, and relies on comparing finite-size calculations (OBC) against bulk formulas (PBC).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram of the QWZ model, the system-size dependence of $\chi_{	ext{norm}}$ for different mass regimes, and the robustness of the diamagnetism against disorder.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the context of divergent diamagnetism in massless Dirac systems, then applying the method to Chern insulators under OBC, contrasting this with PBC results, and finally analyzing the persistence of the divergence under symmetry breaking or changes in filling.
why_interesting: The robust, size-dependent topological response observed here provides a clear, measurable signature (divergent diamagnetism) that distinguishes topological edge physics from bulk properties, which is a key concept in characterizing topological phases.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic correspondence between a one-dimensional ring and a Chern insulator under magnetic flux.

FIG. 2. (a) Phase diagram of the QWZ model as a function of the mass parameter m, together with schematic low-energy dispersions. The phases with 0 < m < 2 and −2 < m < 0 have Chern numbers C = 1 and C = −1, respectively, while |m| > 2 corresponds to topologically trivial phases. The gap closes at m = 0 and ±2. (b) Determination of the orbital susceptibility from the flux dependence of the total energy for m = 1 and L = 16. The values of −χnorm obtained from quadratic and cubic fits are plotted as functions of the maximum flux ϕmax used in the fitting. (c) System-size dependence of −χnorm for m = 1 (Chern insulator), m = 2 (massless Dirac system), and m = 3 (trivial massive Dirac system)....

Figure 2(c) shows the system-size dependence of the normalized orbital susceptibility χnorm for m = 1 (Chern insulator), m = 2 (massless Dirac system), and m = 3 (trivial massive Dirac system). Remarkably, we find that not only the well-known massless Dirac system but also the Chern insulator under open boundary conditions ex- hibits giant diamagnetism, with |χnorm| growing approxi- mately linearly with the system size L. In sharp contrast, for the trivial massive Dirac system, χnorm shows little size dependence for large L and appears to converge to a finite value.

FIG. 3. (a) Energy spectrum under periodic boundary condi- tions as a function of the disorder strength w for m = 1 and L = 48. The bulk gap closes around w ≃3. (b) System-size dependence of the normalized orbital susceptibility −χnorm for several disorder strengths w. The giant diamagnetic re- sponse approximately linear in L persists in the topological regime and is lost in the strongly disordered regime.

FIG. 4. System-size dependence of the normalized orbital susceptibility χnorm away from the symmetric half-filled case. (a) χnorm for several values of the band-asymmetry parameter tasym at half filling. For tasym < 1, where the system remains a bulk insulator, the diamagnetic susceptibility diverges linearly with L, whereas the divergence disappears at tasym = 1. (b) χnorm for several values of α, with the particle number set to N = L2 −αL. For α < 1, the Fermi level crosses the edge states and the divergent diamagnetic response persists, whereas at α = 1 the Fermi level reaches the top of the valence band and the susceptibility tends to a finite positive value.
